Due to mitosis, numbers of cells are increased but the division is strongly controlled, unless some factors interrupt the regulation of cell division and abnormal cell growth occurs, which is named as tumor. Tumor leads to cancer.
A virus named papilloma can cause cancer. Its two virulent genes \( E_6 \) and \( E_7 \) displaces two crucial protein molecules involved in the controlling of cell division. Thus tumor occurs."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Give the comparative analysis between the division of Figure E and F.","marks":4,"answer":"The figure E and F represents meiosis and mitosis cell division process, respectively. There comparative discussion is mentioned below-
- Mitosis
1. Mitosis occurs in somatic cells.
2. The mother cell’s nucleus gets divided to create two daughter cells.
3. Here, nucleus and chromosomes divide only once.
4. The daughter cells have same number of chromosomes as the mother cell.
5. No crossing over event occurs here.
- Meiosis
1. Meiosis occurs in germ cells.
2. The mother cell’s nucleus gets divided to create four daughter cells.
3. Here, chromosomes divide once but nucleus divides twice.
4. The daughter cells get half of the chromosomes compared to the mother cell.
5. Crossing over is important in meiosis.

Thus this process remains controlled. If this control is lost due to any reason, cell division occurs in an irregular way. This results in the formation of a tumor in human body."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"What is happened in 'B' stage of cell division of above stem? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In the above stem, figure-B indicates metaphase stage of mitosis cell division. This stage is explained below—
At the onset of the metaphase stage, all the chromosomes assemble at the equator from the two poles. The centromere of each chromosome remains on the equator but the two arms take positions towards the poles. In this stage, the chromosomes look short and thick. Attraction between chromatids declines and repulsion increases. At the end of this stage, the division of the centromere starts. The nuclear membrane and the nucleolus disappear completely."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Different changes of chromosome perform special contribution to form stage 'A' to 'C'—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"In the above stem, figure-A indicates prophase stage in mitosis cell division and figure-C indicates telophase stage. Different changes of chromosome perform special contribution to form stage ‘A’ to ‘C’.
In the prophase, the nucleolus becomes little larger and chromatin fibers start condensing into short, thick and tightly coiled structures called chromosomes. Though every chromosomes then divides into two sister chromatids, at the centromere they remain attached. Chromosomes remain tangled in this stage. At the pro-metaphase stage the centromeres of the chromosomes become attached to certain attraction fibers. At this time, the chromosomes are arranged in the equatorial region. At the metaphase stage, all chromosomes are initially located at the equator of the spindle apparatus. The centromere of each chromosome is located in the equatorial region and the two arms are positioned towards the poles. Chromosomes are most thick and short during this stage. At the end of this phase, the division of centromere begins. During the anaphase, each chromosome splitting into two, moves to the two poles, and so the number of chromosome remains unchanged. At the end of the anaphase stage, the daughter chromosomes are completely pulled apart to the two poles and start their elongation. In the telophase, chromosomes become decondensed and surrounded by new nuclei. They elongate back into thin and long structures called chromatin fibers and form a mesh called the nuclear reticulum. The nucleolus and the nuclear membrane also reappears. So, ultimately, two new nuclei are formed in the two poles. The spindle apparatus disintegrate and so, the spindle fibers gradually disappear.
So, it can be said that different changes of chromosome perform special contribution to form stage prophase to telophase.
---"}]

Bacteria are single celled microbes. The cell structure is simpler than that of other organisms as there is no nucleus or membrane bound organelles. Instead their control center containing the genetic information is contained in a single loop of DNA. Bacteria reproduce by binary fission. In this process the bacterium, which is a single cell, divides into two identical daughter cells. Binary fission begins when the DNA of the bacterium divides into two (replicates). The bacterial cell then elongates and splits into two daughter cells each with identical DNA to the parent cell. Each daughter cell is a clone of the parent cell. When conditions are favourable such as the right temperature and nutrients are available, some bacteria can divide every 20 minutes."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Which one is more developed between Figure-A and Figure-C? The body of Penicillium is constituted of a single cell or mycelium (narrow tape-like part). On the other hand, the body of bird is multicellular. The nucleus present in the cell of Penicillium is well organized. The cell wall is composed of chitin. But the cells present in bird lack cell wall. The mode of nutrition of Penicillium is absorption. The photosynthetic apparatus chloroplast is absent. However, bird is heterotrophs because there are no plastids in its cells. So it depends on other organism for food. After ingestion, it digests food. It has advanced and complex tissue systems. Sexual reproduction is its usual way of reproduction. Haploid gametes are usually produced in the reproductive organs of mature and diploid males and females. Embryonic layers are developed at the time of its embryonic development. On the other hand, Penicillium reproduces by haploid spores, and its cells divide through mitotic cell division. Meiosis occurs in the anthers and ovules of flowering plants and in the testes and ovaries of animals. Meiosis cell division maintains the purity of a species by keeping the total number of chromosomes constant in an organism. Primordial germ cells of diploid (2n) plants or animals undergo meiosis and produce four haploid reproductive cells. In this process the chromosome number becomes half in daughter cells. Later, the haploid male and female gametes fuse to form diploid zygote which transforms into new organism through repeated mitotic cell division events. Again, zygote of haploid plant undergoes meiosis cell division to produce haploid progeny. Thus, meiosis cell division keeps the chromosome number of a species constant."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"What role will be played by the chart 'B' for our economic development? - Agriculture: Bacteria fix nitrogen in soil, enhancing fertility.
- Food Industry: Used in fermentation to produce yogurt, cheese, bread, etc.
- Biotechnology: Production of antibiotics, enzymes, vitamins, and biofuels.
- Waste Management: Bacteria decompose organic waste, aiding in recycling and pollution control.
- Medicine: Production of insulin and vaccines through genetic engineering of bacteria.
Thus, understanding and harnessing prokaryotic cell division can lead to advancements in agriculture, industry, medicine, and environmental management, contributing significantly to economic growth.

It plays a significant role in the cell division of human body. It is explained below:
The organelle shown in figure A is the centrosome and the process shown in figure B is the mitosis cell division. It plays an important role in cell division. The centrosomes are made from two centrioles. The purpose of a centrosome is to organize microtubules and provide structure for the cell.
In mitosis cell division, during prometaphase, the centrosomes migrate to the opposite poles of the cell. As a result, the mitotic spindle is formed between the two centrosomes. Astral rays spread out from them. After division, each daughter cell receives one centrosome. Due to the presence of centrosomes, cell division takes place.
From the above discussion, it can be said that centrosomes play a vital role in cell division."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"If the process of fig: B is uncontrolled then what problems will occur? These occur due to irregular cell divisions. In mitosis, a cell divides into two, two cells divide into four and so on. This process is regular and controlled. If any problem arises in this division, the cell starts to divide in an irregular, uncontrolled manner resulting in the formation of a cancer cell. Cancer cells or tumor cells are an abnormal mass of cell which develop due to mitotic error.
Various types of germs, chemicals or radioactivity are important for this type of cell division. Even some viruses like papilloma virus is also responsible for cancer formation. Cancer or tumor is a dangerous disease which hampers the normal body function and may cause death. It can develop in any part of the body like liver, lungs, brain, breasts, skin, uterus, etc.
So, we need to be very careful about the risk factors of various cancers and consult with a doctor if any symptom arises.
---"}]

The reactions of the first phase i.e glycolysis do not occur in mitochondria. But the reactions of the second and most important Kreb's cycle stages are performed in mitochondria, as all the necessary enzymes are present. Maximum energy is produced in Kreb's cycle. This is why a mitochondrion is called 'the powerhouse' of a cell."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the differences between figure-1 and figure-2 stated in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Fig-1 refers to mitosis and figure-2 refers to meiosis cell division. The differences between them are—
- Traits: Definition
- Mitosis: Mitosis is the process of cell division which occurs in all types of cells (excluding sex cells).
- Meiosis: Meiosis is the process occurs in the sex cells, which supports sexual reproduction by gametogenesis.
- Traits: Stages
- Mitosis: Prophase, Prometaphase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.
- Meiosis: Meiosis I and II
- Traits: Occurs in
- Mitosis: Somatic cells.
- Meiosis: Germ cells.
- Traits: Number of nuclear division
- Mitosis: There is only one nuclear division.
- Meiosis: There are two nuclear divisions.
- Traits: Type of mother cell
- Mitosis: Mother cell can be diploid or haploid.
- Meiosis: Mother cell is always diploid.
- Traits: Number of daughter cell produced
- Mitosis: There is the production of two daughter cells, which are diploid.
- Meiosis: There is the production of four haploid daughter cells.
- Traits: Chromosome number
- Mitosis: The number of chromosomes remains the same.
- Meiosis: The chromosome number is reduced by half."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Stated figure-2 plays an important role in case of maintaining genetic diversity—Analyze it.","marks":4,"answer":"Figure-2 is meiosis cell division. It plays an important role in maintaining genetic diversity.
Because of meiosis, the chromosome number in organisms remains constant. So generation after generation, the number of chromosomes remains the same in the cells of the body of offspring. Besides, genetic diversity is also found in species of organisms as the exchange of genes occurs during meiosis.
Meiosis transforms a diploid cell into four haploid daughter cells, each having a single copy of each chromosome. The process helps increase the genetic diversity of a species.
During prophase of meiosis- I, the homologous pairs of chromosomes cross over with each other and often exchange chromosome segments. This recombination creates genetic diversity by resulting in chromosomes with a different genetic complement. The exchange occurs between non-sister chromatids. Because genes often interact with each other, the new combination of genes on a chromosome can lead to new traits in offspring.
Fertilization creates genetic diversity by allowing each parent to randomly contribute a unique set of genes to a zygote. While fertilization is not part of meiosis, it depends on meiosis creating haploid gametes. The fertilized cell restores the diploid number. In this way, it maintains genetic diversity.
---"}]

Meiosis helps maintain the uniqueness of a species.
Meiosis maintains the purity of a species by keeping the total number of chromosomes constant in an organism. Primordial germ cells of diploid (2n) plants or animals undergo meiosis and produces four haploid reproductive cells. In this process the chromosome number becomes half in daughter cells. Later, the haploid male and female gametes fuse to form diploid zygote which transforms into new organism through repeated mitotic cell division events. Again, zygote of haploid plant undergo meiosis cell division to produce haploid progeny. Thus meiosis keeps the chromosome number of a species constant. Moreover, genetic diversity is also found in species of organisms as the exchange of genes occurs during meiosis.

Description of this telophase stage is given below—
Telophase is the last stage of mitosis and a reversal of the prophase. Chromosomes become decondensed and surrounded by new nuclei. They elongate back into thin and long structures called chromatin fibers and form a mesh called the nuclear reticulum. So, ultimately, two new nuclei are formed in the two poles. The spindle apparatus disintegrate and so the spindle fibers gradually disappear. At the end of the telophase stage, some small parts from the endoplasmic reticulum aggregate in the equatorial plane and collectively form the structure of the cell plate. Equal distribution of the cytoplasmic organelles is accomplished. As a result, two identical daughter cells are developed. In the case of an animal cell, a contractile ring on the plasma membrane at the equatorial plane pinches off the two nuclei."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Between figure-‘X’ and figure-‘Y’ which one plays important role in creating genetic diversity and survivially of a species in nature?
